turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr Iyer, before the doctor calls you I have checked your observations. Peak flow is three hundred and ten litres per minute, pulse is ninety-eight, oxygen is ninety-six percent, and your breathing is twenty a minute.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Three hundred and ten, okay, I was half expecting worse. I came straight from the office only, my manager is after me for a release, but the breathing was not letting me sit at the desk. The metro from Whitefield was a madhouse today, though that is not your problem.

[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): You have brought two inhalers, so I read the labels as well. The blue salbutamol says one hundred micrograms, and the brown one, beclomethasone, reads two hundred micrograms.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Two hundred? No no, that brown one is one hundred only. The chest physician in Pune wrote one hundred, I remember the prescription. You might be reading the small line, these canisters are impossible.

[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I am reading the strength printed on this canister, two hundred micrograms. I will not argue it, I will leave both inhalers here for the doctor. Kindly have a seat, he is just finishing the previous patient.

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine, fine. Even my cousin, who is a pharmacist in Jayanagar, squints at these labels, and he has been telling me to buy a spacer, which I still have not done. Anyway, that is a side topic.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I am Dr Menon, sorry to keep you waiting. I have the observations that were just taken. Tell me, what brought you in today?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Actually, since this cold, I am wheezing a lot. The cold started maybe ten days back, um, runny nose and all, and that has mostly gone, but the cough was there a bit during the cold also. From Saturday the chest is tight and the wheeze is proper, that is the new part.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Saturday, so about four days of the wheeze and the tight chest, if I am counting right. Is the cough dry, or is there phlegm with it?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly dry, sometimes a little white phlegm in the morning, not green. And when I climb the stairs to the fourth floor I have to stop and hold the rail, which is new for me. Normally I take them two at a time, showing off, which I cannot do now.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this episode? And chest pain, or blood when you cough?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. No blood. Pain as such, no, it is tightness, not a pain pain. My mother keeps calling to ask if I have eaten, she thinks every illness is low sugar, which is a whole other story.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): So no fever, no blood in the sputum, and no actual chest pain, only the tightness. You have had asthma from before, am I right?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Since school, class eight or so. It sleeps for months and then a cold wakes it up. Last year they did that breathing test, spirometry, at a clinic in Indiranagar, and they said it was borderline. They did not give me a number I can remember, just that word.

[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will note the spirometry only as you were told, borderline, not as a figure we can use today. Now the inhalers, tell me how you actually use them, not what the box wishes you did.

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): This is the problem, doctor, I mix up the blue and the brown. When the chest is tight I grab whichever is nearer, and I think the blue is the quick one, wait, or is blue the daily one? No, blue is the relief, I am fairly sure, and I am using that one maybe five, six times a day now, two puffs each time.

[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, blue is salbutamol, the reliever, two puffs when you are wheezy. Five or six times a day is more than I like to see, so I am thinking the airways are still irritable after the virus and the preventer is not covering you. The brown one, are you taking that every day?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): The brown, beclo-something, I am supposed to take it morning and night. Most days I do, but some mornings the stand-up is early and I skip it, so I cannot say I have been regular this week. And I was sure the strength is one hundred micrograms, the staff read two hundred, and now I do not know which is correct.

[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): So we have two strengths in the room and I cannot honestly settle it from memory. I will not put a dose for the brown inhaler in the note until it is confirmed. Keep taking it twice a day if that is what you were told, but the micrograms stay blank.

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. At night I wake once, sometimes twice, wheezing, and then I take the blue one and sit up until it eases. My flatmate thinks I am playing some late playlist, but it is actually me coughing, which is not a useful detail, sorry.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): The night waking is useful, it tells me this is not a small flare. Let me listen to your chest for a minute.

[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): There is a wheeze on both sides, louder on the right, and I am not hearing crackles. You are speaking in full sentences, which reassures me. The oxygen was ninety-six, pulse ninety-eight, peak flow three hundred and ten, and for your age I would hope for higher, though your personal best is not on the file.

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I am thirty-two. Somebody once said my best was four fifty or something, but I am not sure, so please do not write that as a fact. I have a habit of remembering numbers wrongly, ask my cousin.

[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will leave it out. Thinking it through, a viral cold, reliever five or six times a day, symptoms at night, and wheeze when I listen. This looks like an acute asthma flare on top of the cold, and I would not call it pneumonia from what I hear.

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): So not the antibiotic route? My colleague took azithromycin for his cough and he is back in office, and he was pushing me to ask you for the same. I told him I would ask, not that I would demand.

[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am not seeing a reason for azithromycin. There is no fever, the phlegm is not dirty, and the chest is wheeze rather than crackles, so an antibiotic would be treating a guess. What I do want is a short course of steroid tablets, to settle the flare, on top of the inhalers you already have.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Tablets. My uncle was given those once and he said he could not sleep at all, he was pacing the hall. Is it the same medicine, or am I mixing it up?

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): It may well have been prednisolone, and yes it can disturb sleep a little, usually not badly for a short course. I am planning thirty milligrams once every morning, for five days, taken with food. You stop after the five days, there is no need to taper.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Thirty, five days, morning, with food. I can manage that. Should I stop the brown inhaler while I am on the tablets, or is that a silly idea?

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do not stop the brown one. Use the blue when you need it, but if you are still needing it more often than every four hours, or you cannot finish a sentence, or the lips look blue, you go to emergency and do not wait for my clinic. That part is not optional.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Understood, the office can manage without me if it comes to that. Also, my eyes have been itchy since all the dust from the construction beside my building, is that the asthma as well, or am I going off the track? I do that, I know.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Itchy eyes from dust can be the air irritating you, quite separate from this flare, and I will not add a medicine for that today. Before I prescribe the prednisolone, any drug allergies I should know about?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. I have taken penicillin before, no rash, no swelling. Food also, nothing that I have noticed.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good, no known allergy then. One more thing on that old test, was spirometry the only one, or did they also do a chest x-ray?

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the breathing test. They said borderline and told me to carry on with the inhalers, no x-ray. I asked for a printout and the receptionist said the machine does not give one, which I still do not fully believe, but I left it.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, I am not ordering an x-ray today, the story does not ask for one. If the wheeze is not clearly better after the five days, then we repeat the peak flow and we consider spirometry again. For now the plan is the prednisolone, the brown inhaler twice a day, and the blue only when you are symptomatic.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): And the dose of the brown one, you are leaving it blank, yes? I do not want the pharmacy to guess and give me a lecture.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, blank. On your way out, show that canister at the pharmacy counter and ask them to confirm whether it is one hundred or two hundred micrograms, then message the clinic what they say. The salbutamol is one hundred micrograms, two puffs, that part is clear and I am not changing it.

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I will ask them. My mother will only ask me the colour, she knows the blue one and nothing else, so I was thinking I should mark them with tape. Otherwise at two in the morning I will grab the wrong one again.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tape is a sensible idea, write relief on the blue and daily on the brown. I am more worried about that mix-up than about the micrograms, to be honest. If you use the preventer as though it were a reliever, it will not open the airway in the moment, because it is a slow anti-inflammatory, not a quick bronchodilator.

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): So the brown is not for the sudden tightness, the blue is. I think I have been doing it backwards on some days, which explains why those puffs did nothing. Okay, that has gone in, finally.

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me say the assessment in one line so we are aligned. My working impression is an acute asthma exacerbation after a viral cold, not an infection in the lung as far as I can tell. The steroid tablets should start to turn it within a couple of days, though I cannot promise the hour.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): If I am already better on day three, do I still finish the tablets? And you said something about coming back if the five days do not work, I want to get that straight before I forget.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Finish all five days even if you feel well on day three. And book a review with me in one week regardless, so we can recheck the peak flow and sort the brown inhaler dose, not only if you are worse. Reception can give you that slot on the way out.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): One week, even if I am okay. Got it. My cousin's wedding is next month in Kochi and I do not want to be the wheezing person on the flight, so this week actually matters.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then we do this properly. Prednisolone thirty milligrams every morning for five days, with food. Continue the beclomethasone morning and night, dose still to be confirmed, and salbutamol two puffs only when you are wheezy. I am putting the prescription on the system now.

[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I will collect the tablets and I will ask about the canister, and I will try not to skip the morning dose even when the stand-up is early. That is the promise, we will see.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): That morning dose is the one that prevents the next flare, more than any tablet I give you today. Take care, Mr Iyer, and do use the safety net if the breathing turns.

[SEG0049] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr Iyer, if you come to the desk I can book that one-week review for you. I will also point you to the pharmacy counter for the canister check, so it does not get forgotten.
